text: Quality Engineering Assessment: Findings & Improvement Opportunities
Prepared for Comotion (Comotion AI & Seed Analytics) by Bosch Technologies
Comotion AI builds its product and much of its test suite with heavy AI assistance (Python, TypeScript, Next.js,
PostgreSQL), and already has unit, component, and Playwright end-to-end tests — but no dedicated Quality Engineer
owns quality from requirements through release readiness.
Seed Analytics has strict delivery processes, but very little quality embedded within them: test cases are written but kept
outside any test management system, and there is no test automation in the delivery pipeline.

Comotion AI's engineering team is clearly comfortable using AI to accelerate both feature development and test creation, and
this has produced a genuinely useful base of unit, component, and end-to-end tests. However, without a dedicated Quality
Engineer, no one is accountable for whether that AI-generated test suite actually reflects requirements, how reliable it is, or
whether it provides enough confidence to call a release "ready". As the codebase and AI usage grow, this gap will widen rather
Seed Analytics presents the opposite profile: a disciplined delivery process with almost no testing substance behind it. Test
cases are written diligently but are not stored anywhere searchable or reportable, and there is no automation protecting the
pipeline from regressions. This leaves the team fully reliant on manual effort for every release, with no scalable way to increase
release frequency without proportionally increasing manual testing effort.
A shared Quality Engineering capability — tailored to each entity's starting point — would give Comotion AI the governance and
measurement it currently lacks, and give Seed Analytics the foundational tooling and automation it has not yet built. Over time,
this also allows the group to report on quality and release readiness consistently across both entities.
A shared Quality Engineering function with clear ownership of quality across both entities.
Comotion AI: quality embedded from the requirements stage through release readiness, governed AI-assisted test
creation, increased coverage, and CI/CD quality gates producing a measurable release readiness signal.
Seed Analytics: all test cases held in a test management system, with a CI/CD automation foundation (built on the group's
existing Playwright standard) acting as a regression safety net.
Group-wide quality metrics and release readiness reporting, visible to engineering and leadership.
